state_open: Open at {url}, for this machine only.
state_closed: Closed: no application or tool can reach AIODOS.
apps_title: Open AIODOS to applications on this PC
apps_help: An application (PANDORA, ARKLIGHT PC…) asks for access on its own: a card appears, you compare the code and choose what it can do. The first access you grant opens AIODOS to applications.
requests_help: When off, applications already allowed keep working, and new ones are refused without a card.
same_account_title: Refuse applications from another Windows account
same_account_help: Each app's program and account are checked on every request.
general_key_help: Give it to the tool as its “API key” (it sends it as “Authorization: Bearer …”). It stays the same from one launch to the next; once renewed, the old one stops working at once. For a tool, a manual key (above) has its own permissions: that's better.
addresses_help: Models: the name alone (qwen3.5:9b) lets AIODOS choose the machine that answers; “peer:…” names one. Step by step for each tool: docs/autres-outils.md.
stdio_title: Assistant that launches a program (Claude Desktop…)
stdio_help: Add it to the assistant's MCP configuration (claude_desktop_config.json…): the bridge reads the address and the key by itself. AIODOS must be running, with the gateway open.
general_help: Open WebUI, AnythingLLM, Continue, a code editor or an MCP assistant (Claude Desktop…) can then use this machine's models and the ones your paired machines lend you, and search your libraries. The passages found go to the assistant, and to its model: to the cloud if it's a cloud model. Libraries kept on this PC (the padlock) are never shown to them.
port_help: Fixed: the address doesn't change from one launch to the next (11435 by default, next to Ollama's).
renew_text: Tools that use the current key won't be able to reach AIODOS until you give them the new one. The assistants' bridge (Claude Desktop…) picks it up again by itself.
